layers.name: Layer 1: Structural signals
layers.intro: Each signal has: what it decides, how to detect each STATED value, the proposal move per value, and a defined FALLBACK move for when the post says nothing. The fallback is a real instruction, never a blank.

layers.name: Layer 2: Domain and capability signals
layers.intro: Each signal: stated values + detection, proposal move per value, and a defined FALLBACK for silence.

layers.name: Layer 3: Hidden signals
layers.intro: The read-between-the-lines layer. NOT keyword-matchable — the phrases below raise probability, they don't prove. Each signal has its stated tells, the proposal move, and a defined FALLBACK for when the post gives no tone signal (the majority case here). for every hidden signal, "neutral/no tell" is the MOST common outcome. So the fallback is not an edge case — it is the default path the system takes most of the time. Make it strong.
layers.rule_note: Score each hidden signal as a probability. When two or more point the same way (rescue pain + guarded + value), that combination dominates the voice. When ALL are neutral — the common case — fall back to: specific, calm, senior, one clear next step. That neutral-default voice is the backbone the system uses most often, so it must be strong on its own.

signals.name: Who they want
signals.decides: whether to front a team or a single named lead engineer.

values.name: Agency / team
values.detect: "agency", "small team", "development/engineering team", "dev shop", "capacity", "bandwidth", company-level references/profile requested; or scope one person plainly can't deliver.
values.move: present Stackup as a team with a named lead; emphasise capacity and coverage across roles.

values.name: Solo / individual
values.detect: "independent contractor", "freelancer", "individual", "one person", "work autonomously", "self-directed"; first-person "I want someone who", availability/hours questions.
values.move: front ONE named senior engineer; personal ownership, direct line to you.

values.name: Both ("developer or small team")
values.detect: names both explicitly.
values.move: lead with a named person, mention team depth as backup.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: nothing stated — this is 51% of posts
values.move: front a named senior lead engineer AND state a team stands behind them. This wins solo-leaning posts without losing team-leaning ones. Never guess "solo" or "agency" from silence.

signals.name: Engagement model
signals.decides: the commercial framing of the proposal.

values.name: Fixed
values.detect: "fixed price", "milestone-based", "one number", stated total budget + defined deliverable.
values.move: give a confident fixed structure with clear milestones.

values.name: Hourly / ongoing
values.detect: "/hr", "hourly", "hrs/week", "ongoing", "retainer", "long-term", duration fields ("1 to 3 months"), "maintenance".
values.move: propose a rate + an ongoing engagement; emphasise you stick around post-launch.

values.name: Discovery-first
values.detect: "discovery phase", "workflow assessment", "architecture phase", "independent estimate", "scope before budget".
values.move: lead with a small paid discovery step as the entry point.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: nothing stated
values.move: propose the engagement structure YOU recommend for the work described (usually a short discovery step, then ongoing), framed as best practice. Lead the framing rather than matching a signal that isn't there.

signals.name: Project maturity
signals.decides: whether the proposal opens with a build plan or a diagnosis.

values.name: Greenfield / MVP
values.detect: "from scratch", "greenfield", "new product", "build the MVP", no mention of any existing system.
values.move: open with a confident build path and a clear MVP scope.

values.name: Rescue / extend
values.detect: "not a greenfield project", "already have", "existing", "previous/last developer", "take over", "migrate", "broke", "not working", "inspect", "refactor".
values.move: open with diagnosis — "rebuilds like this fail because X, here's how I avoid it."

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: nothing stated — 55% of posts
values.move: open with ONE light diagnostic line that works either way ("First thing I'd do is confirm what's already in place before touching anything"). This reads as senior on a greenfield post AND correct on a rescue, so you never assume wrong.

signals.name: Positioning axis
signals.decides: whether the voice leads with architecture or business outcome.

values.name: Technical
values.detect: "architecture", "infrastructure", "pipeline", "backend", "multi-tenant", "RAG", "vector", "senior engineer", "hands-on".
values.move: lead with senior technical depth and how it's built.

values.name: Product / outcome
values.detect: "client-facing", "own the relationship", "consultant", "strategy", "outcomes", "go-live", "discovery with leadership".
values.move: lead with business results and ownership, prove technical depth after.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: nothing stated
values.move: default to TECHNICAL voice (58% of the pipeline is technical, only 2% purely product), but include one outcome sentence early so a product-minded reader is covered.

signals.name: Structured submission demanded
signals.decides: whether format compliance is a pass/fail gate. (No fallback needed — this signal is binary and always readable.)

values.name: Yes
values.detect: "generic proposals are not read", "answer the following", "include the word X", numbered required sections, mandatory attachments.
values.move: follow the structure EXACTLY, first, before anything else. Deviation = auto-reject.

values.name: No
values.detect: open-ended "share your experience", no structure specified.
values.move: use your own strongest structure.

signals.name: Vertical / industry
signals.decides: which proof story and case study leads the proposal.

values.name: Real estate
values.detect: MLS, realtor, listings, property management.
values.move: lead with the matching vertical proof story. Education now needs its own dedicated case study.

values.name: Healthcare
values.detect: patient, clinic, dental, dermatology, EHR, HIPAA, aesthetic, physician.
values.move: lead with the matching vertical proof story. Education now needs its own dedicated case study.

values.name: Legal
values.detect: law firm, attorney, personal injury, case management, paralegal.
values.move: lead with the matching vertical proof story. Education now needs its own dedicated case study.

values.name: Construction/trades
values.detect: HVAC, contractor, remodel, handyman, roofing, plumbing.
values.move: lead with the matching vertical proof story. Education now needs its own dedicated case study.

values.name: Logistics
values.detect: freight, fleet, dispatch, supply chain, carrier, load board.
values.move: lead with the matching vertical proof story. Education now needs its own dedicated case study.

values.name: E-commerce
values.detect: Shopify, Amazon, Walmart, order processing.
values.move: lead with the matching vertical proof story. Education now needs its own dedicated case study.

values.name: Insurance/finance
values.detect: underwriting, final expense, annuity.
values.move: lead with the matching vertical proof story. Education now needs its own dedicated case study.

values.name: Education
values.detect: student, tutor, course, coaching, recruiter, career platform, advisor. (NOW A PRIORITY — 2nd biggest at 13%)
values.move: lead with the matching vertical proof story. Education now needs its own dedicated case study.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: no vertical — 57%, the majority
values.move: treat as HORIZONTAL business automation. Lead with breadth and a cross-industry proof, and make reusability a selling point. This is not a gap — most of your pipeline is genuinely horizontal, so horizontal is a first-class route with its own strongest general proof.

signals.notes: named in title or first 2 sentences, else inferred from workflow

signals.name: Core capability
signals.decides: which competency to foreground. Most posts stack 2+.

values.name: Voice
values.detect: receptionist, phone, inbound/outbound call, Retell, Vapi, Twilio, IVR.
values.move: record ALL that apply; foreground the PRIMARY (title or most-words). Automation and full-stack SaaS are the two spines to nail first.

values.name: RAG
values.detect: knowledge base, retrieval, vector DB, Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector, embeddings.
values.move: record ALL that apply; foreground the PRIMARY (title or most-words). Automation and full-stack SaaS are the two spines to nail first.

values.name: Agents
values.detect: AI agent, multi-agent, autonomous, LangChain/LangGraph/CrewAI.
values.move: record ALL that apply; foreground the PRIMARY (title or most-words). Automation and full-stack SaaS are the two spines to nail first.

values.name: Automation
values.detect: automate, n8n, Zapier, Make, RPA, integration, workflow. (82%, dominant)
values.move: record ALL that apply; foreground the PRIMARY (title or most-words). Automation and full-stack SaaS are the two spines to nail first.

values.name: Full-stack SaaS
values.detect: multi-tenant, platform, dashboard, Next/React/Node/Laravel, MVP, portal. (74%)
values.move: record ALL that apply; foreground the PRIMARY (title or most-words). Automation and full-stack SaaS are the two spines to nail first.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: capability unclear
values.move: read the workflow. "Automate our operations" = automation. If still unclear, default to automation + full-stack SaaS (the two that cover most of the pipeline) and describe a general build.

signals.name: Named stack & tools
signals.decides: which exact tool names to reflect back as proof.

values.name: Named tools
values.detect: any named product/language/framework/API captured verbatim (GoHighLevel, n8n, Zapier, Twilio, Vapi, Retell, Next.js, React, Node, Python, Postgres, pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant, Claude/OpenAI, Salesforce, HubSpot).
values.move: name each tool back and cite a project using it.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: no tools named
values.move: propose your recommended stack with a one-line justification each. Silence here is permission to lead — do NOT stay vague.

signals.name: Compliance & sensitivity load
signals.decides: how much the proposal must sell safety and process. This splits the pipeline ~50/50, so treat it as a primary branch, not a detail.

values.name: High
values.detect: HIPAA, PHI, patient data, NDA, "confidential", "sensitive", on-prem, local hardware, data residency, GDPR.
values.move: add a dedicated reliability/security paragraph; when HIPAA + local processing, make it a top-three theme.

values.name: Low / none
values.detect: no security language.
values.move: one light reassuring line, no more.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: ambiguous
values.move: include one brief security-and-reliability sentence by default. Cheap insurance; never costs you on a low-compliance post.

signals.name: Data & scale intensity
signals.decides: whether this is a serious engineering buyer who sees through fluff.

values.name: High
values.detect: "millions of records", high volume, exactly-once, dedup, TTLs, distributed, multi-tenant isolation, "not a CRUD app".
values.move: name the hard part back to them, show real depth fast, engage the TRUE hard part (data/pipeline), not the AI.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: not stated — 80%
values.move: assume normal scale and do NOT over-engineer the pitch. Keep the proposal outcome-focused rather than infrastructure-heavy unless a scale tell appears.

values.name: Rescue / frustration
values.detect: "last/previous developer", "not working", "broke", "failed", "done right this time", "unreliable", over-specifying what NOT to do.
values.move: name the pain in the first line; open with diagnosis and reassurance.

values.name: Fresh / opportunity
values.detect: excitement, "building", "new product", no past-pain mention.
values.move: lead with the vision and a confident path.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: neutral — 80%
values.move: open with quiet competence — a specific, concrete observation about their actual project that proves you read it. No manufactured empathy, no assumed pain. Specificity IS the hook when there's no emotional tell.

values.name: Founder
values.detect: "I want", "my company", "our business", "we are a [business]", emotional stake.
values.move: speak to their business outcome, reassure the person.

values.name: Middleman
values.detect: "our client", "on behalf of", "do not contact", white-label, staffing/agency framing.
values.move: make THEM the hero to their client; emphasise you are low-risk and easy to manage.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: unclear — 53%, and hides most real middlemen
values.move: write to the person as if they are the owner, BUT keep it easy to forward — professional, low-drama, no over-familiarity. This covers both a quiet founder and a hidden middleman without betting on either.

values.name: Value
values.detect: "most experienced", "senior", "expert", "willing to pay", "quality", "actually shipped", "proven".
values.move: lead with depth and senior proof; do not discount.

values.name: Price
values.detect: "affordable", "tight budget", "cheap", "low maintenance" (note: low-maintenance can be pragmatic-quality, a good buyer).
values.move: decide compete-or-skip; usually skip pure price buyers.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: neutral — 35%
values.move: assume value-leaning (only ~1% are openly price-driven). Lead with quality and seniority by default; never open by competing on price.

values.name: Precise
values.detect: numbered scope, deliverables, explicit tech choices, "must include", defined constraints.
values.move: CONFIRM understanding and show exact execution; don't re-explain their own spec.

values.name: Vague
values.detect: "figure out", "not sure", "open to ideas", "help us", "explore", "identify where".
values.move: LEAD — show the path, propose discovery, turn their fog into a plan.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: neutral — 67%
values.move: take gentle leadership. Restate their goal in one crisp sentence to show understanding, then propose a clear first step. Works whether they were secretly precise or secretly vague.

values.name: Guarded / burned
values.detect: "generic proposals not read", "disqualified if", "do not contact", strict rules, NDAs, long requirement lists, "must".
values.move: acknowledge their rules, follow them visibly, sell reliability/process BEFORE skill.

values.name: Open
values.detect: casual, trusting, "open to suggestions", few rules.
values.move: respond with warmth and ideas.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: no strong tell
values.move: default to calm, professional, process-aware — show you are safe to hire without being defensive. Neutral-professional never alienates an open client and reassures a quietly guarded one.

values.name: Ready
values.detect: "start immediately", "ASAP", "this week", fixed near-term deadline, "hiring now".
values.move: close with confidence and a concrete fast start plan.

values.name: Nurture
values.detect: "budget discussed later", "evaluating", "exploring", "getting estimates", "down the road".
values.move: offer a low-friction next step (call/discovery); don't hard-close.

values.name: Fallback
values.detect: neutral — 92%, i.e. almost always
values.move: Urgency is essentially unreadable from Upwork text, so do NOT infer it from the description. Default to a confident-but-not-pushy close: one clear next step, no false urgency. Pull real urgency from job age / invites / client activity elsewhere, not from this layer.

signals.name: Invite
signals.decides: whether the proposal answers an invitation (the Invite type).

values.name: Invited
values.detect: "Personal note from client", "invite only", "I invited you", "you were invited", or the post addresses the freelancer by name.
values.move: Use the Invite type: thank them briefly (by name if given), two lines on why you fit, one question.

values.name: Not an invite
values.detect: nothing says the freelancer was invited.
values.move: Write as a normal application.

signals.name: Role seniority
signals.decides: whether the client wants a builder or an architect, lead or consultant (the Architecture or consulting type).

values.name: Architect or consultant
values.detect: title words "architect", "principal", "lead", "consultant", "auditor", "advisor"; asks for strategy, a roadmap, an assessment or a review.
values.move: Write as the person who owned and decided: the trade-offs, the risks, and how you would assess first.

values.name: Builder
values.detect: nothing beyond building is asked.
values.move: Write as the builder: what you would build first and why.

signals.name: Scope size
signals.decides: how long the proposal is: a small bounded task gets the Small fix type.

values.name: Small task
values.detect: one bug, one change or one small feature; a few hours; a small fixed budget.
values.move: Keep it short (50 to 100 words): what you would do, how soon, one question.

values.name: Platform
values.detect: many modules or roles, a long term build, a large budget.
values.move: Show the structure: phases, and the team behind you.

values.name: Project
values.detect: anything in between.
values.move: A normal length proposal.
